newsitem.title: UK: British truckers relieved port blockade lifted.
newsitem.headline: British truckers relieved port blockade lifted.

text.p: Up to 400 truck drivers stranded on a motorway near the British port of Dover on Thursday prepared to move their vehicles after striking French fishermen suspended their blockade of Dunkirk, Calais and Boulogne.
Many of the drivers had slept in their trucks during the night and were delayed up to nine hours waiting for cross-Channel ferries.
"Four hundred trucks are queued up. We are working to clear part of the motorway," a police spokeswoman said, adding that two sections the motorway had been closed because of the congestion.
The 18-mile (29 km) long traffic jam began on Tuesday after the French fishermen began their protest over European Union regulations on net sizes.
A spokeswoman for the port of Dover said ships were leaving for Calais. The authorities hope all the trucks will be on ferries by the end of the evening.
"It will take a long time to clear the trucks," a spokeswoman for AA Roadwatch said, adding that it would be impossible to say when traffic would be back to normal.
The French fishermen lifted their blockade as they met with Agriculture Minister Philippe Vasseur to try settle their dispute.

Normally, 2,000 trucks a day take the ferries between Dover and Calais, a journey of about 90 minutes. The trip to the Belgian port of Zeebrugge, to which ferries have been diverted, takes more than four hours.
